area: Dress Up: the deep ocean, a world of its own under the surface ocean, with diving
text: A deep ocean world, dived into from the surface ocean. N, via Matthew: "another world (deep ocean) that is accessible from the surface-style ocean squares, where we swim on the surface. I recommend separating the few deep ocean squares we have onto another world (called deep ocean) --- let's replace the deep ocean with more surface ocean and separate into another world, somehow --- with a vertical way of connecting worlds together between surface ocean and deep ocean, something similar to the 'hole' in the cemetery, except not localized to one spot, and not rendered as an object. Not sure where to place the 'nav' arrow, but it would be nice to actually center it below the person as they swim, to indicate that every spot offers a chance to dive." And: "diving animation, maybe just a variation of swimming?" Plan: the start world's 🪸 deep sea squares become 🌊 open water; a 🪸 deep ocean world under it, a square under every open-water square (the old deep squares' things kept there); from any open-water square, a ⬇️ arrow centred under the swimmer dives to the square below; from the deep ocean, ⬆️ above them swims up. A dive: the swim, head down, sinking; coming up, the reverse.
source: Matthew in the Code session, 2026-11-09 afternoon ("dress-up time."), N's ask.

area: hazel, hazeljs: a JS object's keys in another order than the labeled tuple's fields gets stuck when a field is a list
source: Found by Claude, 2026-11-06 11:24, building matthewhammer/hazeljs-petri-example (Matthew's ask, the same day): its Node example passed the net's view as {transitions, marking, draw} and every answer came back {hazel: ...}.
text: Bug in hazeljs 0.0.4 (#2719's library): key order matters for a labeled tuple with a list field. Hazel.run("fun (p : (x = Int, y = [Int])) -> p.x").value gives 5 for {x: 5, y: [1]} but {hazel: "...(Asc ..."} for {y: [1], x: 5}: stuck at the parameter's annotation. With only Int fields ({y: 3, x: 10}) the order does not matter. A JS object's keys have no order a JS developer thinks about, so the boundary should convert by the type's field order (or by label), not the object's. Where: the library's value conversion in (JS object to labeled tuple), and the cast it meets; check whether #2681 (no cast re-checked at run time) or ^ticket(681) (converting JS values directly) changes it. Until fixed: hazeljs-petri-example's node/petri.mjs builds its view in Net's field order and says why.
